answer.question: What should I know before requesting turf for a Holly Hills address?
answer.answer: Holly Hills is in unincorporated Arapahoe County even when the mailing address says Denver. Confirm the parcel and applicable county requirements, then bring any property documents to the estimate. Show us the space you want to change and the landscape that will stay.

blocks.h2: Change the part that is hardest to use.
paras: A patch beside the patio, a dog’s route or a putting line can define a useful project without replacing all the planting. Mark trees, roots and irrigation before the old lawn comes out. Include any low spots and the route for materials in the visit.
For a green, choose the putts you want and leave room to stand and walk. For pets, consider cleanup access and shade alongside the turf boundary.

blocks.h2: Use the parcel, not the mailing label.
paras: Ask Arapahoe County about the actual scope if the proposal includes grading, drainage or other landscape changes. Check any recorded property or association requirements as well.
Use the provider on your water bill when comparing ongoing costs. A nearby Denver program should not be assumed to apply simply because the address is written the same way.

blocks.h2: From 1 October, Denver Water's rules turn the sprinklers off.
paras: Denver Water sets the watering rules at your address, even though the bill arrives from the Holly Hills Water and Sanitation District. Denver Water lists that district as a Total Service distributor, so it owns the pipes, reads the meter and bills you directly (Denver Water). Water questions go to Denver Water; the district keeps its own operator for the sewer (Holly Hills Water and Sanitation District).

The 2026 Stage 1 drought declaration holds from 25 March 2026 through 30 April 2027 and asks for at least 20% less water (Denver Water). Through 30 September, even-numbered houses water on Sundays and Thursdays and odd-numbered houses on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and never between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. (watering rules).

From 1 October, watering grass and running spray irrigation are prohibited, and breaking the rule brings violations and charges. A synthetic lawn looks the same on 2 October as it did in July, with no controller to shut down and no brown patches to wait out.

The sewer half of the bill stays where it is. The district sets sewer charges from your winter water use in December, January and February, which keeps summer irrigation, water that never reaches the sewer, out of the figure (Holly Hills Water and Sanitation District). Watering less in the yard shows up on the Denver Water side only.

blocks.h2: Arapahoe County sets the rules here, not Denver.
paras: Holly Hills is 371 acres of unincorporated Arapahoe County with the City and County of Denver on every side (Holly Hills). Your address may read Denver, 80222, but the County, not the city, is the land-use authority for your yard.

That makes Arapahoe County Public Works and Development the office to ask, and its code answers part of the question already. A fence needs a permit from the PWD Building Division before it goes up, is altered or moves, and the section says it is written to reach fences that form a boundary between properties or enclose more than 15 percent of a lot (Arapahoe County Land Development Code, Section 4-1.5). Where it applies, a fence in front of the house is held to three feet and one at the side or rear to six. A short panel inside the yard for a dog run may fall below that 15 percent line, so ask the Building Division which side of it your plan falls on before you order materials.

The county's water-efficient landscape standards are aimed elsewhere: parks and open space, new development or redevelopment, and non-residential expansion. Their cap on turf is written for new single-family projects, and the code defines turf as cool-season grass, Kentucky bluegrass and fescue (Arapahoe County Land Development Code, Section 4-1.4 and Chapter 7). Nothing in the code names artificial turf either way, so ask the Planning Division to confirm in writing that your yard sits outside those standards before the layout is final.

The state's turf law doesn't touch a home lawn either. SB24-005, as amended by HB25-1113, bars local governments from allowing non-functional turf in new commercial, institutional and HOA common-area projects, and single-family yards sit outside it (SB24-005, HB25-1113). Our guide to Colorado's turf law walks through it.

blocks.h2: Flat ground, Front Range clay, and whatever the lawn left behind.
paras: Holly Hills sits at 5,476 feet on flat to very gently sloping ground, so grading is simple. The clay underneath is the Front Range kind: the Colorado Geological Survey says its montmorillonite and bentonite clays can expand by up to 20% when wet, at pressures to 30,000 psf, and about one in ten homes built on expansive soils is damaged over its life (Colorado Geological Survey).

What's under the grass matters too. A lawn that's been watered for years can leave old sprinkler lines, deep thatch and big surface roots from shade trees, so the free site visit looks for all of it before the old lawn comes out.
Then comes the base, built for this clay and graded to carry water away from the house, since cracked drives, walks and foundations are what the Survey says swelling clay usually breaks.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Holly Hills, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial lawns, putting greens for practice and pet turf in Holly Hills, CO. Holly Hills is unincorporated Arapahoe County, even with Denver on every side, and Denver Water’s 2026 drought rules end grass watering here on 1 October. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Does any water rebate cover turf in Holly Hills?
faq.a: Not for turf. Denver Water's published residential rebates cover toilets, up to $100, and qualifying sprinkler heads, and its Landscape Transformation Assistance Program is for business customers (Denver Water). Resource Central's lawn replacement program, a Denver Water partner, requires the new landscape to be at least 50% waterwise plants, which turf can't meet (Resource Central).

faq.q: Can I still water my trees after 1 October?
faq.a: Yes. Denver Water's 2026 Stage 1 rules keep hand-watering with a shutoff nozzle and drip irrigation legal for trees and shrubs after 1 October; it's grass watering and spray systems that stop (Denver Water).

faq.q: Do I need a permit or HOA approval for turf in Holly Hills?
faq.a: Ask the County first. Holly Hills is unincorporated, so Arapahoe County Public Works and Development is the review authority, not Denver, and its Land Development Code is the code that applies to your yard (Arapahoe County Land Development Code). Then check your title papers for an HOA or plat covenants. If there is an HOA, Colorado law bars its design guidelines from prohibiting nonvegetative turf in the back yard of a detached single-family home (SB23-178).

faq.q: Does a turf lawn count toward lot coverage in unincorporated Arapahoe County?
faq.a: The county's code defines lot coverage as the part of the lot under buildings, including overhanging roofs, and under parking areas (Arapahoe County Land Development Code). A lawn is neither, so swapping grass for turf doesn't move that figure. Grading, drainage or a retaining wall is a separate question for Public Works and Development.
